newsitem.title: UK: Stan Chart shares fall, denies loss rumours.
newsitem.headline: Stan Chart shares fall, denies loss rumours.

text.p: Shares in Standard Chartered Plc fell sharply on Friday amid broker rumours the bank had sustained losses on Asian currency dealings as a result of the currency turmoil in the region.
But the bank firmly denied there was any substance to the speculation, which saw Standard Chartered shares fall 36.5 pence to 968.5 pence by 0956 GMT, a fall of 3.43 percent.
"There is nothing in it whatever. It is all rumour," a Standard Chartered spokesman told Reuters.
"The rumour in the market is that they lost a substantial amount of money in currency dealings, but the company has denied it," one analyst confirmed.
Another theory for the fall was that the stock had recently been driven to record highs by general buying of the bank sector and the drop was due to profit-taking.
One banking analyst said the shares had moved up too fast in the last few days, but were not supported by the factors which had prompted buying of the mainstream UK banking stocks.

This was the result of the protection from sterling's strength afforded by the British banks and the scope for consolidation in the domestic sector, neither of which applied specifically to Standard Chartered, he added.
But Standard Chartered's exposure to the Asia-Pacific region was also highlighted as an area of concern.

ABN AMRO Hoare Govett banking analyst Peter Toeman said there were concerns about the weakness of the Malaysian ringgit and the fact the government may continue to use interest rates to support the currency.

Malaysia contributed 40 percent of Standard Chartered's pre-tax profit of 241 million stg from the Asia Pacific region, out of a total of 870 million stg last year, and fears were that possible interest rate rises may slow down GDP growth, with a knock-on effect on bank lending.
